setup: Stand on one leg, knee soft
execution: Push off sideways from the outside leg
Land softly on the other foot
Hold the landing, knee over the toes
Then bound back the other way
faults: Don't land with a straight knee
Don't let the landing knee cave in
Don't jump forward instead of sideways

notes: Bound on a non-slip surface with clear space on both sides.
Start with short bounds and a 1–2 second hold on each landing; add distance and speed once landings are steady.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain at the knee or ankle on landing
Pain that changes how you move

regressions.name: Lateral step and stick
regressions.reason: Step sideways onto one leg and hold, with no flight.

regressions.name: Short lateral bound with a hold
regressions.reason: Small bounds with a full stop on each landing.

progressions.name: Continuous lateral bounds
progressions.reason: Bounce straight into the next bound with a short contact.

substitutions.name: Broad jump
substitutions.reason: Jumping power in a straight line.

guideBrief.cameraNote: Front view at hip height so the sideways travel and the landing knee's line over the foot are clear. Leave room on both sides of the figure.

keyPositions.label: Load
keyPositions.describe: Standing on the right leg, knee and hip bent, chest slightly forward, left foot off the floor. Arms back to swing.

keyPositions.label: Flight
keyPositions.describe: Pushed off the right leg, body travelling to the left, both feet off the floor, arms swinging across.

keyPositions.label: Landing
keyPositions.describe: Landed on the left leg about a body-width or more to the side. Knee bent and over the toes, hips back, right foot off the floor behind. Held still.

ikHints: Landing knee tracks over the second toe
emphasise: Sideways push from the outside leg
Landing knee in line with the foot
